works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: We Are Not Given a Short Life
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. I–II — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: Seneca's thesis: Nature is not stingy — life is long enough if you know how to use it. We do not receive a short life; we make it one.

works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: Putting Off Life
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. III — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: The folly of deferral — men promise to begin living once they reach fifty or sixty, and so postpone life until it is nearly spent.

works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: The Engrossed Have No Time to Live
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. VII — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: A gallery of the busy: drunkards, the over-groomed, the legacy-hunters, the restless — occupied with everything except the art of living.

works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: The One Thing Worth Guarding
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. VIII — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: We defend our money and estates fiercely, yet let anyone help themselves to our time — the one possession it is honourable to be greedy with.

works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: At Leisure with the Great Minds
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. XIV–XV — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: Only those who give their time to philosophy truly live; they may sit with Socrates, the Stoics, every age — and add all the centuries to their own span.

works.section: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE)
works.title: Past, Present, and Future
works.source: On the Shortness of Life, ch. XVI — Aubrey Stewart translation
works.note: The busy forget the past, neglect the present, and dread the future; the past is the one secure part of time — but they have no leisure to look back on it.
